records.question: How many orders are in the dataset?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders

records.question: How many unique customers have placed an order?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.customer_unique_id) AS unique_customers FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id

records.question: How many sellers are based in the state of São Paulo (SP)?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS seller_count FROM sellers WHERE seller_state = 'SP'

records.question: What is the average review score?
records.sql: SELECT AVG(review_score) AS average_review_score FROM order_reviews

records.question: How many orders were canceled?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS canceled_orders FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'canceled'

records.question: How many payments were made with each payment type?
records.sql: SELECT payment_type, COUNT(*) AS payment_count FROM order_payments GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY payment_count DESC

records.question: What is the most common number of instalments for credit card payments?
records.sql: SELECT payment_installments FROM order_payments WHERE payment_type = 'credit_card' GROUP BY payment_installments ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, payment_installments ASC LIMIT 1

records.question: How many orders were placed in 2017?
records.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM order_purchase_timestamp) = 2017

records.question: How many reviews were given at each review score?
records.sql: SELECT review_score, COUNT(*) AS review_count FROM order_reviews GROUP BY review_score ORDER BY review_score;

records.question: What is the total payment value for each payment type?
records.sql: SELECT payment_type, SUM(payment_value) AS total_payment_value FROM order_payments GROUP BY payment_type ORDER BY total_payment_value DESC

records.question: Which 5 customer states placed the most orders?
records.sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(o.order_id) AS order_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_state ORDER BY order_count DESC LIMIT 5

records.question: On average, how many items does an order contain?

records.question: How many orders were placed in each month from January to August 2018?
records.sql: SELECT strftime(order_purchase_timestamp, '%Y-%m') AS month, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders WHERE order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2018-09-01' GROUP BY month ORDER BY month

records.question: How have sales trended month by month?
records.sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS month, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count, SUM(oi.price) AS total_sales FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE o.order_purchase_timestamp IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

records.question: What percentage of customers are repeat customers?
records.sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE order_count > 1) / COUNT(*), 2) AS repeat_customer_percentage FROM (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS order_count FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.customer_unique_id) t

records.question: What share of delivered orders arrived later than the estimated delivery date, by month in 2018?
records.sql: SELECT strftime(order_purchase_timestamp, '%Y-%m') AS month, COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders, SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS late_orders, ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN order_delivered_customer_date > order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS late_share_pct FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'delivered' AND order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL AND order_purchase_timestamp >= TIMESTAMP '2018-01-01' AND order_purchase_timestamp < TIMESTAMP '2019-01-01' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

records.question: What was the month-over-month revenue growth rate in 2018, from February to August?
records.sql: WITH monthly AS (SELECT strftime(o.order_purchase_timestamp, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(oi.price) AS revenue FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE EXTRACT(year FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) = 2018 AND EXTRACT(month FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN 2 AND 8 GROUP BY 1) SELECT month, revenue, (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)) / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month) * 100 AS mom_growth_pct FROM monthly ORDER BY month
records.reason: no predicted column matches gold column 'growth_pct'

records.question: Do late deliveries get worse reviews? Compare the average review score of late and on-time delivered orders.
records.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 'late' ELSE 'on_time' END AS delivery_status, COUNT(*) AS order_count, AVG(r.review_score) AS avg_review_score FROM orders o JOIN order_reviews r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY delivery_status ORDER BY delivery_status

records.question: Among product categories with at least 1,000 reviewed orders, which 5 have the lowest average review score? Use English names.
records.sql: WITH oc AS (SELECT DISTINCT oi.order_id, COALESCE(t.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category FROM order_items oi JOIN products p ON p.product_id = oi.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation t ON t.product_category_name = p.product_category_name) SELECT oc.category, COUNT(DISTINCT r.order_id) AS reviewed_orders, AVG(r.review_score) AS avg_review_score FROM oc JOIN order_reviews r ON r.order_id = oc.order_id WHERE oc.category IS NOT NULL GROUP BY oc.category HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT r.order_id) >= 1000 ORDER BY avg_review_score ASC LIMIT 5

records.question: Among customer states with at least 1,000 delivered orders, which has the highest late delivery rate?
records.sql: SELECT c.customer_state, COUNT(*) AS delivered_orders, AVG(CASE WHEN o.order_delivered_customer_date > o.order_estimated_delivery_date THEN 1.0 ELSE 0.0 END) AS late_delivery_rate FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_customer_date IS NOT NULL AND o.order_estimated_delivery_date IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.customer_state HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1000 ORDER BY late_delivery_rate DESC LIMIT 1

records.question: What share of total revenue comes from the top 10% of sellers?
records.sql: WITH seller_rev AS (SELECT seller_id, SUM(price) AS rev FROM order_items GROUP BY seller_id), ranked AS (SELECT rev, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY rev DESC) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER () AS n FROM seller_rev) SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN rn <= CEIL(n * 0.1) THEN rev END)::DOUBLE / SUM(rev)::DOUBLE AS top10_pct_seller_revenue_share FROM ranked

records.question: For customers who ordered more than once, what is the average number of days between their first and second order?
records.sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT c.customer_unique_id, o.order_purchase_timestamp, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id ORDER BY o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS rn, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY c.customer_unique_id) AS cnt FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id), firsts AS (SELECT customer_unique_id, MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 1 THEN order_purchase_timestamp END) AS first_ts, MAX(CASE WHEN rn = 2 THEN order_purchase_timestamp END) AS second_ts FROM ranked WHERE cnt > 1 GROUP BY customer_unique_id) SELECT AVG(date_diff('day', first_ts, second_ts)) AS avg_days_between_first_and_second_order FROM firsts

records.question: Which 5 product categories grew revenue the most from 2017 to 2018? Compare January to August of each year, in absolute terms, using English names.
records.sql: SELECT COALESCE(t.product_category_name_english, p.product_category_name) AS category, SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(year FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) = 2018 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) - SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(year FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) = 2017 THEN oi.price ELSE 0 END) AS revenue_growth FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id LEFT JOIN category_translation t ON p.product_category_name = t.product_category_name WHERE EXTRACT(month FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) BETWEEN 1 AND 8 AND EXTRACT(year FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) IN (2017, 2018) GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY revenue_growth DESC LIMIT 5
